utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dosenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Ivetic, I also put on the record that Mr. Mladic is back in court, and you may continue your examination-in-chief and I think ten minutes was what was left. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, as you heard, we have ten minutes so I'd like to briefly touch on a few points that we still have remaining in our examination. In this case, this Chamber has heard claims that both channels of a duplex transmission of a voice conversation over a radio relay device were able to captured by either the ABiH southern or northern posts with the explanation given that when a participant does not press the headset against his ear, sound from the headset speaker travels to the microphone and thus is able to be transmitted on the same channel as speech into the microphone. Can you comment briefly on the technical aspects and science of such a claim.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, they are theoretical claims. I have never heard of any practical or mathematical proof that that could happen. The basic thing is that it cannot go that way because there is a filter that prevents the two from mixing, these two channels that is. Secondly, military telephones, all military telephones, are conducted in such a way that on the headset or on the receiver there is a plastic frame and if the receiver is a few centimetres away from the ear, it is no longer possible to hear the speaker well. And then also there is this transformer that separates the two, not only in terms of entering VF but also every further level at radio relay devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could now take a look at the document from the southern location, and it should not be broadcast. It is 1D01081.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for it, I think we will see it is again a listing of equipment and listening stations that were at that location. And in relation to the first two on the list which are work positions 3 and 4, I see that both have a parabolic and antenna, an SO 42 converter, and the various receiver and transceiver devices. Is such an antenna, receiver, and converter setup suitable for listening to radio relay devices used by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see R100. They could have received VH -- no, UHF, FM 200 that is. The splitter, okay. Then this SO 42, that would be superfluous because these are lower frequencies. And this parabolic antenna is not right for receiving. The parabolic antenna I saw in the photographs are for 2.5 gigahertz. Whereas devices where the -- that the Army of Republika Srpska had, had transmitters that work from 4.4 megahertz onwards. So I do not see the point of a parabolic antenna, either for 3 or 4, work station 3 or 4. As far as I could see in the photograph, too, where these parabolic antennae are, picture number 1, this antenna is fixed to the pole and its degree is about 30 -- its angle is about 30 degrees and that shows that it had a fixed route along which it worked, if it did in the first place, and then this participant was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you there for a second. Mr. Ivetic, the witness is referring to photographs. It's not entirely clear what photographs he is referring to. They're not on our screen at this moment. And I don't know whether it has been established that what we read here is in any way related to what can be seen on a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, he mentioned photograph 1 which I believe is photograph 1 from his report which Your Honour have marked for identification and it is on page 54 of the Serbian original. As the photographs are only in the Serbian original not in the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see where ... the witness said: "The parabolic antenna I saw in the photographs ..." So apparently there is more than one photograph involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There's one on the next page as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So it's a reference to photographs he commented upon in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the second issue was whether those photographs are linked to what is described here on paper. Could you perhaps also pay attention to that when either putting in between questions or later on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I could just see where we left off.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just, please, complete your answer as to what you were saying about the parabolic antenna before we go on to the next point.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in photograph number 1, it is visible that the antenna is fixed to the antenna pole and that its degree is about -- its angle is about 30 degrees and 2.5 gigahertz. There weren't such devices in the Army of Republika Srpska. And in view of the positions, the altitude held by the VRS, the antenna could possibly be in a negative angle, about 5 degrees. So in my view, these antenna did not operate vis-à-vis the VRS devices. They were intended for something else, for receiving something from someone else. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's first deal with the SO 42 converter. At this trial, Witness RM-279 on transcript page 13507 of our transcript said in relation to these converters as follows: "Our equipment was not professional. First of all, we had to raise frequency to 16.000 megahertz, I believe, to use as a zero base-line. So it's not the same base-line for our devices and military devices. We had to raise the signal. These are all makeshift converters." Sir, what is your professional opinion and comment as to what this witness is saying here as for the need to use SO 42 converters?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SO 42 converters are supposed to lower frequencies from a high frequency to a lower frequency; never from a lower to a higher frequency. And I need -- I see no need for this kind of converter here. Actually IC-R100 could just receive RRU-800 and the 200 device.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can turn to the next page in Serbian and it will be page 3 in English, we will see three other listening posts, 5, 6 and 7, connected to two Yagi antennas and a quad antenna using the IC-2G, the M.Kobac, and RUP-12 devices. Can you tell us briefly, yes or no, can these listening posts as configured listen in on radio relay unit transmissions by the VRS again as configured?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here for listening posts 5, 6 and 7 we see three devices, an IC-2G, an M.Kobac, and an RUP 12 which are connected to a Yagi, a Yagi, and a quad antenna. Can these listening posts using this equipment effectively listen in on radio relay transmissions of the VRS, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, these are devices to be used on VVF and also on single-channel equipment. I did not find any material about intercepting VVF communications so the existence of this equipment does not really mean much to me. And also you can see the Kobac set and you can see that it was defective; that is to say that it was not being used. RUP 12 with an amplifier of 300 watt and this antenna and that was used for different purposes. 20 to 70 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender the document at this time. Under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D01081 receives Exhibit Number D1199, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1199 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And one final area to address what Your Honours raised. If we can have D00308 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while we wait for that, sir, this is another photograph and it is represented to be from the southern location as to whose documents we have been -- as to whose document we have just had on the screen now. And, sir, with respect to this parabolic antenna from that location, is there anything to your prior answer that you need to add or describe now having the photograph of the actual antenna before us?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a parabolic antenna. In some documents that I received from the lawyer, I saw that somebody stated that this was handmade, hand manufactured. That is impossible. This is a parabolic antenna and electromagnetic waves are received here and it further transmitted through the pole sticking out of the antenna. The construction of the receiver on this antenna is quite heavy so good experts would have to work on these calculations and especially one would require very good machines to get this antenna in such a polished state so that it can receive and transmit waves, so I doubt that this was done by hand. Why somebody said that, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, for the record, it was at transcript page 13596 that a witness described this as a handmade parabolic device.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Last question. If you could explain for us, in your prior answer as to the use of parabolic antennas to listen to the VRS transmissions, you indicated something about how a negative -- let me just get the terminology right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps when you are considering your next question. Witness, do you have any knowledge about what machinery they would have available to polish the parabolic antennas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these concave dishes or, rather, parabolic antenna, I did not see their actual manufacturing. I'm not sure, however, that they would have that -- well, let's say they could make an antenna, but this receiving part on the antenna for receiving the electromagnetic waves that are later transmitted, I am almost certain that they did not have the material required for that or a man who could do the right arithmetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What machines did they have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know which machines they had, Your Honour. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you say, It requires specific machines to do it, and I doubt whether they had them, you just don't know whether they had them or not. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the former Yugoslavia, not a single factory machined these antennae. All of them were imported, primarily from Siemens in Germany and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's nice as an explanation, but you just don't know what machines they had to produce it themselves if they wanted to do that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, that's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, does it look very much as an industry-produced parabolic antenna? Is this what you would expect if it comes from a factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is how you would expect it to come from a factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in your prior answer, you talked about document -- photograph number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So I think to have that on the screen, I think the original photograph is P01649.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, in your answer you say: "... that in photograph number 1, it is visible that the antenna is fixed to the antenna pole and that its degree is -- its angle is about 30 degrees and 2.5 gigahertz. There weren't such devices in the Army of Republika Srpska. And in my view, the positions, the altitude held by the VRS, the antenna could possibly be in a negative angle, about 5 degrees. So in my view, these antenna did not operate vis-à-vis the VRS devices. They were intended for something else, for receiving something from someone else." Could you now explain for us what you meant when you said that in view of the positions and altitudes held, there could possibly be a negative angle. Is what we see here a negative angle? Could you explain what you meant by that, that comment, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that such antennae, on the assumption that they can receive something from VRS devices, over here it should be horizontal. We know how high up this is, so because of the altitude difference there has to be a bit of a negative angle because these antenna are very sensitive. An angle of 5 or 6 per cent, that's not really a tolerance that exists. That's what I was trying to say the first time as well. Now, who they could receive something from we can only go into assumptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you if you are expressing yourself on the angle, angle in relation to what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the pole and the antenna make up an angle, primarily looking at this pole that is sticking out, so then the angle that it comprises with the antenna carrier, that it is to say that it is attached to, the antenna itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean to say whether it's just above-horizon directed or below-horizon directed or -- horizon, I should say, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I said it's a bit above horizon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would you agree with me that the impression you can have from such a photograph fully depends from the angle under which it is photographed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is how I see it in this photograph. I used a protractor to measure the angle and it's about 25, 30 degrees. If I take a zero axis or, rather, this pole at 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I you think -- you do not think that the angle under which is all photographed may deceive any measurement because it's bringing three dimensions back to two dimensions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the carrier and the antenna are under the same angle -- I mean, the photograph was taken from the same place and that is why that tells me that all of these angles are real ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I think if you measure the angle on a photograph, the outcome is exactly the same as you would measure the angle in a real three-dimensional situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, apart from tendering the marked for identification report and any other of the figures that are contained therein, we have no further questions for the witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic, as far as the SO 42 is concerned, you are aware that was quite a bit of a discussion at the time about what is a normal SO 42, how it was used, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All details which were unable, I take it, for this witness, unless the witness has read that portion of the transcript, that it was a rather complex matter which was reduced by you to what looked a simple matter. I leave it to that but just for you to know that that's what is my recollection of the SO 42 discussion with the other witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think the part that I read from the transcript actually was part of that discussion and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, a very small part of a very complex discussion. I just leave it to that for this moment. Mr. McCloskey, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, everyone, Mr. President. I hear the witness, I think, wants to make a comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. He's entitled to do so, but before he does, one second, please. First of all, in a minute, you'll be cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey. You find Mr. McCloskey to your right. Mr. McCloskey is counsel for the Prosecution. But I do understand that you wanted to make a short comment. Would you please -- please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would only like to make one correction to my testimony from Thursday. I made a slip of the tongue when you asked me from whom I got the information about the KZU-1. It was not Zivko Dzenopoljac. It was the man from whom I received command, Mr. Suslevic. He now works in Travnik in an installation for communications. I can explain this slip only by the fact that I had a fit of kidneys from the previous night, from 10.00 at night to 5.30 in the morning, and I really suffered a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that may have affected the accuracy of your -- only of this answer or in general of your answers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my recollection, I made only that one mistake. I wanted to correct it immediately but then I was under pressure. Later I was terribly tired and I forgot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For that explanation. Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if I could spend a very brief amount of time on parabolic -- if we could go back to P01649 on parabolic, yeah, antennas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yesterday you may recall that on page 37802 of the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it was on Thursday, not yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Oh, there was a weekend. Yes, thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Judge Orie asked you this question when you were talking about these antennas. He said: "Witness, could you tell us what would be the diameter needed for a parabolic antenna intercepting any signal under 1 gigahertz, what size, therefore?" And your answer was: "Technical calculations are made for that, but in my estimate, I believe that the dish would need to be approximately 2 metres in diameter, even 2.5 metres." So you stand by that, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Judge, it's 2.5 gigahertz not gigabytes. Those are two different units of measurement. I did not make any calculations of the diameter of these antennas, but I know from experience the diameters of the devices that can operate on up to 2.5 gigahertz and the diameters of ones we used in the JNA that are from 4.4 gigahertz. And I did not present any precise values, I gave you the rough ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, my -- we don't want to be here forever, I just asked you if you stood by your answer to Judge Orie. So the -- do you stand by that answer?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm just a lawyer so you don't need to refer to me as "Your Honour." Though I understand. Now, I want to take you briefly to a comment that one of the supervisors of the interception sites said. It happens to be in this case at page 13623. And he is talking about various things, and intercepting with antennas, and he states on line 18, in part: "We believe that this signal was received by reflection when it bounced off mountains. In other words, we were not within the beam where this radio relay route would be dispersed." And so is that correct, can they sometimes intercept a radio relay communication that is bouncing off or reflecting off mountains or other large objects?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we have cases here that it reflects from an object on the ground and features on the ground. However, these beams usually disperse. Those that receive reflections are those that are reflected from layers of the atmosphere. They can be received well and they can be separated clearly from these. Those are the only signals at that frequency that would be reflected from the atmosphere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, it was a simple question. Can sometimes radio signals be received if they bounce off mountains, not directly in the beam?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I said such signals cannot be received because they disperse. Only if they would hit a large metal table would they be possibly well received. The signals reflected from features on the ground could not be received because they would immediately disperse, disappear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the witness goes on to say: "Perhaps to clarify further, in order to receive a quality signal, we had to install a mountain antenna, a parabolic antenna, a huge antenna of some two metres in diameter on the mountain." So here we have agreement between you and the Muslim witness that you would need a big two-metre parabolic antenna; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He must have gotten information from someone that he needs such a large antenna to receive the frequencies they estimated were being used by the VRS. They must have gotten information from someone at which frequencies the VRS worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The question is: You and this man are in agreement about the size of the parabolic antenna needed; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object to the question. Needed for what? Can we have a ruling on the objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was clear, but if you would again put the question to the witness, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, the witness said yesterday at 37802 in response to Judge Orie's question: "Technical calculations are made for that. But in my estimate I believe that the dish would need to be 2 metres in diameter. Even 2 and a half metres." And we remember the context that that was in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this was to receive any signal below 1 gigahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so you both agree about the size of an antenna in this context? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we agree on the size of the antenna. But I said, in particular, for each belt you have to make a calculation of the dish and especially the active element of the dish, the thing you see on the photograph as a cylinder. That has to be calculated with maximum precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And to try to be clear, you have not read any transcripts of trial testimony from this case from any Muslims, BiH, MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think I will again object because we're mixing transcripts and testimony. As counsel is aware, in this Tribunal, in this courtroom, transcripts are not the only type of testimony and so we need to be rather precise to make sure that the witness understands the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there's no -- if there are other sources which the witness may have read, that's fine. But Mr. McCloskey is asking about transcripts of trial testimony and that's clearly defined. And whether there's more evidence, that's a different matter. Witness, did you ever read any transcripts, that is, verbatim reports of what witnesses said in this courtroom in this court, that is, before the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, only from Nedo Blagojevic. No one else, neither from the BH army, nor the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, you just told us -- you mentioned the battalion commander of the Drina Corps. Did you read his trial transcripts or something else as well?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked at it on a diskette, but only partly, when Jevdjevic was here. Only a part of it, not the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you read part of Milenko Jevdjevic, the commander of the Drina Corps communications battalion, you read part of his trial transcript but not the whole thing; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I watched. I did not read. I watched the recording of the trial here on a diskette.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you watch the cross-examination of Mr. Jevdjevic?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That is unfortunate. All right. How about Veljko Pajic? Who is that? Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not meet that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you never reviewed any transcript of Witness Pajic or saw it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And roughly how many actual transcripts of intercepted conversations did you review for your report and testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can be sure about ten to 15, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what units were noted in those intercepts that had received those interceptions?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I saw, the names are mentioned of officers holding positions in the Drina Corps and the Main Staff. I once even read a reference to the Bratunac Brigade, the Zvornik Brigade. I did not really pay attention to the units they were from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, those are the units of the people talking on the intercepts. What my question was: Which unit actually took part in the intercepting? Normally, on most of them, it's written on the top of the intercept.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you well, sir, you are asking me which unit organised and practiced the interception of the communications of the Army of Republika Srpska. Is that the question? From what I see from the available materials, it was a reconnaissance company of the 2nd Corps of the BH army based in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, that's a start, but my question was the actual intercepts themselves. Did you distinguish the actual unit that had received the intercept?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I wasn't looking for it. I wasn't interested in whether it was installation 1 or installation 2. As for the other units, since I was in the 2nd Corps, I knew they had units in the 5th Corps of the BH army, but I didn't have the opportunity to see a single transcript of their intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you didn't notice if those intercepts you read were from the 2nd Corps or perhaps the state security of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina or perhaps the 21st Division of the Army of the BiH?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These transcripts that I told you I've read, they certainly come from the reconnaissance unit of the 2nd Corps of the BH army. And the first one I read concerning intercepts on the telephone at the very beginning of the war, that was from the MUP, the Ministry of Interior, because from what I could establish, only the MUP dealt with intercepts of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I note the time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Time for a break. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes when we'll continue. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, if you are ready, you're invited to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Sir, let's go to your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's our number D1187, page 30 in the English, page 43 in the Serbian or B/C/S. And, yes, this is not to be shown as with most of these things. Thank you. Thank you. We don't need that parabolic antenna anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I want to -- I'll read this slowly, it's short. It's paragraph 10.9. And you say in your report, and I quote: "The types of devices available to the BH army led me to the conclusion that they were able to monitor all our radio and radio relay communications maintained through RRU-800, FM-200, and through single-channel devices." Now when you say "single-channel devices," is the RRU-1 included in that description?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, RRU-1 and RDM -- RRU-1 is Yugoslav made and the other one is Czech made --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to interrupt you --

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- are the only radio relay pieces of equipment that are single-channel devices and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my question. But we only have so much time and the simple answer that you got to was: Yes. We didn't need to know who manufactured them and all that. That's already part of it. So I know you're trying your best, but try to focus on the question and a simple answer. And when you need to explain an answer. You will always be allowed to do that, I think, almost always in this courtroom. So, anyway, that's just something to help get us through. Okay. So you stand by this paragraph in your report, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I'm not quite sure whether your question was answered, does it include the RRU-1?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I started interrupting him and camouflaged the answer. That's my fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you -- Witness, can you answer the Judge's question. As the -- does the single-channel devices referred to in this paragraph include the RRU-1?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And I apologise for making that difficult. You go on to say: "Written documents transmitted by the mentioned devices were encoded so that they could not work out the content." Now, if written documents were sent via these radio devices and were not encoded, for some reason someone didn't do the coding correctly or decided to send it in the open, then they could -- those documents could be intercepted, could they not?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, everything that that was sent through this equipment could be listened to by those who had listening devices, coded and uncoded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So a document that was sent through these devices uncoded could be intercepted, you know, by the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anybody can intercept it if they have devices with the right frequency, Muslim side included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's clearly distinguish. Once intercepted, they could directly read it if it was uncoded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to 65 ter 32425, and as we're waiting for that, as you have told us, you were the chief of communications for a good while during the war at the 2nd Krajina Corps. That's right?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the beginning until the end, including a short break in 1992, the end of 1992 and beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you didn't do any work over in the Drina Corps' zone or over in the area around Zvornik, Vlasenica, Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went there during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We see this document, and you can see the whole thing because it's all in the -- in the Serbian. If we look at the second page in the English, we can see that it's from your commander, Colonel Boric, and let's go back to the first page. We see it's June 27th, 1992, 2nd Krajina Corps, and this is a general order. And it states: "There is reliable information that the HVO forces, the Green Berets, and foreign military forces are intensively tapping all kinds of radio-relay, radio, and radio-telephone lines. They are also tapping the lines going through the PTT system. Thus, by electronic reconnaissance and line tapping, the enemy reveals very important intelligence on combat activities, firing positions of our artillery weapons, manoeuvre, preparations for combat activities, morale of our units, and similar information." And the -- do you confirm that the enemy intercepting all these sorts of communications was a real problem in June 27th -- in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, concrete consequences, as a result of that, we didn't see any. However, it's always a problem if information leaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah. Sir, I didn't ask you if they were concrete problems as a result of this. I just asked you if it was a problem the -- the enemy was intercepting your communications. Do you confirm that this was an actual problem as Boric says it was, or do you think he's wrong?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, orders are issued when it is noticed that there are such occurrences, in order to prevent them from happening in the first place or perhaps be reduced to a minimum, because there's always people who do not observe each and every rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you're telling us is that the document shows that it was a problem. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That it was noticed that there are cases that somebody speaks in the open through communications, but it's not that it's a massive thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it says "intensively," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly. That's always to be expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, I checked with one of my colleagues. The translation where it says "the enemy reveals very important intelligence on combat activities" might need some attention because what one would expect as logic in this context would be that the enemy receives very important intelligence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Or that there are investigations that reveal that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or -- or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- the enemy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, whatever it is, but could you have the translation verified because the understanding of document as it is now creates at least some problems. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I agree and understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, my big -- my point was do you agree that this was a problem? Do you agree with what this document says? We can see that the document says that they're intensively doing this but do you agree? You were there, you were the comms guy.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that was not a major problem and it wasn't that this order was written on account of that. There was certain things that happened and then an immediate reaction followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. McCloskey. It's clear what the document says. The witness says that it was -- you are discussing size of the problem rather than whether there was a problem. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there a significant problem of the enemy intercepting the communications of the VRS in 1995, in June of 1995, in your area, as far as you knew it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very beginning until the end of the war, we knew that the enemy and everybody else was always following our communications, and our attention always focused on the prevention of information leaking through our communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I would offer 65 ter, the last document, 32425 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Given what Your Honours have said about the translation, I think we should mark it for identification at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic, perhaps you are in a position to already cast a first impression on whether there may be such a mistake or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I can't assist you with my degree of fluency in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it will be marked for identification pending verification of the translation. And if the translation is okay, Mr. McCloskey, then we'll further hear from you what the gist of the message then is. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 32425 receives Exhibit Number P7499.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Any need to have it under seal? Not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we have P07058 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, this is -- the reason I asked you the question about June 1995 is that we have, as you'll see, a document coming up that is in the name of General Mladic from the Main Staff dated 17 June 1995. And we see that it's addressed to the commanders of the various corps, including the 2nd KK, your corps. And General Mladic says, in the English, it should be -- B/C/S page 1, it's the first page of the English, three paragraphs up: "According to the information available, the enemy is persistently and very effectively using secret military information obtained by intercepting our radio and [sic] radio relay post, telephone and telegraph communications." Do you -- from your knowledge of what was going on at the 2nd Krajina Corps and any study you've done, do you agree with General Mladic that this was a problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object as to the context of the question. The actual third paragraph provides the details which I think are fair to provide the witness with if they're going ask about what was being complained about because they are specified in that paragraph differently than the paragraph that was read by Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He has the full document. He can take a look at it. It is a simple question, do you just -- do you agree with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, apparently, let me see. One second, please. The witness may answer the question. If you want to give further context and ask further questions, Mr. Ivetic, you have an opportunity to do so in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Sir, once again, could you please repeat your question. I was reading the document so I did not quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you agree with General Mladic that the -- that this is a problem, that the Muslims are getting effective use of information that is being given or received by them? It talks about sloppy behaviours on the part of the VRS, other things. Just asking you: Was this a problem that you saw in your corps?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as far as I can see in this document, it is public security centres that are mentioned so it's not only the military but also the population. Communication through communications equipment. That information was leaked that way. Now whether all of that was received, I mean, by the intelligence organs of the BH army --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That wasn't the question, whether it was received. Could you please focus on the question. Do you agree that -- with General Mladic that the enemy is persistently and very effectively using secret military information obtained by interception and whether that was a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It constituted a certain problem, but not of proportions that would affect the combat readiness in the units of the Army of Republika Srpska significantly. It wasn't only the BH army that was listening. Others around the territory of the Army of Republika Srpska were listening too, and information was provided to those who needed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on. Let's go back to your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: D1187, should be page 33 in the English, page 48 in the Serbian. And this should not be broadcast. I've got the English correct but, I'm sorry, I don't have the B/C/S correct. It must a page earlier. It's ... there it is, yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And it should not be broadcast. Oh, yes, you said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see that, here, in your report, you talk briefly about the southern intercepting site and you, in your first paragraph, note that it's a mountain. And you give the distances between various places, between Vlasenica, Veliki Zep, and other places we've heard. Next paragraph, you talk about decibels and another topic. And then in that third paragraph, 10.16.8, you say: "There is no optical line of sight between ... the southern site and Zvornik, and there is no optical line of sight between the southern point and Vlasenica. The logical conclusion of the rule [sic] is that where there is no optical line of sight, there is no interception." Now, where do you get that information that there is no optical line of sight between the southern site and Vlasenica, for example?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this is not mere information. This is a scientific finding. Radio relay communications. It would mean if you don't see me, you don't hear me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That wasn't the question. The question was: On what basis you present that there was no optical line of sight between the two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no optical visibility. When you take a topographic map, when you monitor the altitude where the facility in the south is and where this other location is, then you will see that there is no optical visibility and therefore there is no radio visibility either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and my question was: Where did you get this conclusion, how did you come to this conclusion? Did you do this calculation yourself? Are you relying on someone else? You give no citation. There's no footnote here. There's no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, for the fact of the absence of any line of visibility or for the conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The conclusion that there is no line of sight between Vlasenica and the southern --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we should clearly distinguish between the fact, that is, whether there is a line of sight, and the other is what conclusions can be drawn if there is no line of sight, but you're focusing exclusively on the first item.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely. Thank you. The other one I will probably leave to others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But this basic, simple line of sight issue, how did you come to it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, what was accessible to me was the radio visibility between the stations south and north and facilities where there were radio relay stations and nodes and so on. Now that's where this information comes from and I also checked it myself on a map, 1 to 100.000, and there is no radio visibility, and also I have all the radio relay routes recorded as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So is the elevation of the southern site and the elevation of Vlasenica important in determining whether there is, in fact, optical visibility between the two?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's important is the fact whether there is any obstacle between them and also distance matters. In this case, there is an object obstacle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is the elevation of Vlasenica important as one of the things to determine whether there's anything blocking it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. If Vlasenica is lower than the obstacle between them and the north installation, of course, there would be no visibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So tell me, as you worked out your conclusion that there was no optical visibility, what elevation did you give for Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know off the cuff. But you can see on the map exactly what the altitude is. You can -- with an error of 20 metres minus or plus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see from the first paragraph in this report that you said the southern mountain was at 1326, which is the position of the Prosecution that is the height, but you can't tell me now the elevation that you used for Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know off the cuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, let me then ask you. You reviewed the report of a man named -- a Serbian man named Rodic, Djuro Rodic. He wrote an expert report for the Popovic Defence that you have cited. In this case, it's at 65 ter 1D05805. He also had an annex to his report, 1D058 -- excuse me, 1D00322. And he did this report back on the 23rd of April, 2007. Now, since you have -- you'll agree with me you've cited his report for various things?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Djuro Rodic, whether he's a Serb or not. I had access to his analysis but without any attachments. And as can you see from my paper, in some places I referred to his analysis, to the facts that are accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did you read his complete report?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could read, I think it was entire. But without any attachments, without annexes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, you cited Mr. Rodic's annex at page 22 in the English and page 29 in the Serbian in your report. In our footnote, it's called "supplementary material."

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, did you or did you not review Rodic's supplementary material, his annexes? We see you citing it in your report. You just said you didn't. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I received is connected into one, and it's certain that there is another part called "annex." I didn't say that I didn't read that part but I said without attachments such as schematics, maps, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. Let's go to D1187, your report again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This time page 32, the page previous in English and the -- it should be page 46, I believe, in the Serbian. So let's go to 46 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we see now we're talking about -- you're talking about the northern site. And did you figure out the line of sight between this -- the northern site and Vlasenica and other locations yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I looked at a map on a scale of 1 to 100.000, but there was no need for me to do that and to draw, in particular, because I received from the law firm the positions of all these radio work stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My question again is: As in what you've testified in the southern site, did you figure this out yourself, line of sight, for this site and the other locations, or did you rely on someone else's work?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, not exactly precisely 1 to 100.000. But when I compared the profiles received from the law firm, I did that precisely. It's not something I did for the first time. I made profiles a hundred times in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you did it yourself. You didn't rely on Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether these profiles I received were made by Mr. Rodic, I don't know. I don't think it's written on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The question was: You did this line of sight for this northern site yourself, you did not rely on Mr. Rodic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't working alone. I told you I relied on the documents received by the law firm, but I don't know whether they were done by Djuro Rodic or somebody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There may be some confusion. You said you received documents from the law firm. Did that include the profiles you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't receive everything at the same time. I would receive one piece now, another thing later. Not -- not everything in a batch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask you whether you received it at the same time. I asked you whether in the materials you received, whether the profiles were included.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Among other things, once when I was taking documents, I received also profiles. But nobody told me who made them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did you again, you yourself, do the same job; that is, to create profiles independent from the profiles you had received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I checked one or two of these profiles. I told you, I had many profiles myself, hundreds, so I didn't find it necessary to check all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And how did you check the one or two you checked? Did you do that by constructing your own profile and then compare them or by looking at the profile and then assessing whether or not it would be okay, or in any other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the method I used for checking whether it's accurate was by using a thread to see whether the two points can be connected and whether there's an obstacle, whether there's visibility. That's how I -- that's how I checked the profile. I didn't check the whole profile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On the basis of what documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said you connected the points and established if there's an obstacle or not. What did you use to -- in order to establish this finding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the map, I would connect two points there using a thread to see whether there was visibility. There was no need for me make a new profile myself. You can see that immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you do that with respect to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Using a ruler. I did it for all radio relay routes mentioned in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could intervene. We have at line 24, the prior page, the addition of using a ruler which I don't know where that relates to. In the B/C/S that was used, but it was used in relation to the prior answer, so I don't know that we have in the English the full extent of the witness's answer to Judge Fluegge's question in precisely the same order as it was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have received the answer I wanted to receive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still am a bit -- you said you verified two of the profiles, one or two, and you did it not by recreating the whole profile, but you looked at a map and you thought it was okay, using a ruler. All the others, as you said, you did not verify. Now, I think the question of Judge Fluegge was: Was the Vlasenica profile, had the connection with Vlasenica, was that one of the one or two that you verified or did you take it for granted that it would be okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I checked the routes about which they told me there was no optical visibility, which were said not to have optical visibility. I didn't check the others. And that's three or four radio relay routes mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's from one to two now to three or four. But let's, Mr. McCloskey, I leave it in your hands. And what I do not fully understand is that we're talking about connecting one point to another point from a certain elevation. The other point at a certain elevation as well. And then to find out whether there's any obstacle in between, an obstacle which, if it is on the top of the mountain, you would expect from natural things rather than buildings, et cetera. Why couldn't the parties agree on that, whether there is such --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't realise it was in dispute. I actually cut out a whole bunch of questions that I was going ask the witness to demonstrate that for us on the belief that the Prosecution was not contesting that there was no visibility from Zvornik and Vlasenica, but it can be shown. I mean, the witness can be asked and he can demonstrate. I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think you can do it yourself, I mean, and show it to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, what you need is a map, you need the exact location of the one and the exact location of the other, and there may be a difference of 20 metres because the elevation lines on the maps may leave some margin. And then draw the line and see whether there any elevation line which goes higher --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, you also need one other element which is the curvature of the earth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So there's another graph that needs to be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Only if the distance requires so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For short distances, not. For longer distances, that may be the case, but for the short distances not. That's a matter -- and it also, of course, depends on how high the mountains are. If the mountains are 10.000 metres high, then you have less problems with the curve of the earth for certain distances.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Depending what's between them, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I really do not see why we have to spend such a long time where it seems to be a rather mathematical issue to be resolved between the parties. The witness is somewhat unclear at this moment in what he did and what he didn't do. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey. One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, that is the theme of my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and your focus was to find out from this witness what he exactly did and what he didn't do. Okay. And that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you've said that "they" told you. I don't see exactly where it was now, but you said "they" told you that -- what sites had optical visibility and you didn't look at those. When you say "they," who are you referring to? Who told you about optical visibility?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember using the word "they," but I wrote exactly here between which points there is no optical visibility, and that is sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, you said in line 18, page 37: "I checked the routes about which they told me there" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please speak closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "I checked the routes about which they told me there was no optical visibility, which was said not to have had optical visibility. I didn't check the others." So who were you referring to when you said "they" told you?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I say again, I didn't say "they." I said the points about which I saw from the profiles I received, there is no optical visibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's just briefly look back at your document. Now, did you receive Rodic's report from the Defence or did you get it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already made that statement. I received all the documents from the law firm and the information about the resources I got from the Internet. Those are my only sources, apart from general knowledge from various rules, encyclopedias, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you receive Rodic's report from the Defence? That was the question; nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't hold it against me, but if you include the law firm in that, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What you did mean by "law firm"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean Mr. Ivetic, Mr. Lukic, and the others who work there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We refer to them as Defence. You received Rodic's report from the Defence. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And let's see what's in front of us now where you cited Rodic's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We need to go to the next page in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And looking at paragraph what's called 10.16.4, you conclude: "From the radio-relay interception stations [sic] at the northern site, there is no line of sight towards Vlasenica and Zvornik, which makes interceptions of communication on that route impossible. From the station at the northern site there is optical and radio visibility towards the nodes at Veliki Zep, Cer, and Crni Vrh."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Redaction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the northern site, did you do the northern site towards Vlasenica yourself or did -- are you relying on Rodic as you did the northern site to Veliki Zep?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I did not do a single complete profile myself. Only on the map I drew a line using a ruler from one point to another, and I can notice immediately whether there are any obstacles or not. I am very well-versed in this. I had done that a hundred times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah. Sir, my question was: Did you rely on Rodic to do that, as you cite him here for this particular paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm going object to the question as being vague. He went from a specific question to now a vague question. He has been talking about Vlasenica, Zvornik, Crni Vrh, Veliki Zep, and the last one which I can't think of off the top of my head. We've heard that the witness did verify some and some he did not. So if we want to have an answer that will be meaningful --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection for the argument. I will try to rephrase it. I was trying to save a little time. I think it's evident from in front of what we're talking about, but I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not. You say this particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, please, please. The objection is moot because Mr. McCloskey has offered to rephrase his question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And looking at paragraph 10.16.4, looking at the last sentence, you state: "From the station at the northern site there is optical and radio visibility towards the nodes at Veliki Zep, Cer, and Crni Vrh." And you cite to Rodic. So are you relying solely on Rodic for that conclusion or did you do it yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not myself, not alone. Based on Rodic's work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In fact, for your opinion regarding the southern site and Vlasenica, you relied on Rodic as well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. But I checked myself as I mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And as I think you'll agree with me, the -- as you already have, the elevation in Vlasenica is very important for this analysis, and you've said you checked the map to get that elevation of Vlasenica. What part in Vlasenica did you use to get the elevation? What section of town?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statement of the commander of the communications battalion who told me at one meeting where the radio relay station in Vlasenica was, but whichever part of town were it to be located, and it wasn't in town, you can't have radio relay communications because there are obstacles that are much higher, including more than several dozen metres higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, you just said you had a meeting with who?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion, I met Jevdjevic at -- in Banja Luka, at the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was the Defence with you?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic Jr. was there; Sasa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how long did this meeting last between you, Jevdjevic, the former commander of the Drina Corps communications battalion, and yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't alone with Jevdjevic. There were other people. And I don't know all the people from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How long did this meeting last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was there -- did you see someone taking notes at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did Jevdjevic tell you where the building in Vlasenica -- where the radio relay site was in Vlasenica during the war time?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, but I asked where his position was. He told me approximately. I don't know Vlasenica, but in any case, wherever you placed it in Vlasenica, you cannot have communications. There is no visibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he tell you it was on the building of the Drina Corps? Did you tell you how high the building was?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Nothing specific. He just said it was in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you don't know where in Vlasenica the radio relay node was and you don't know if it was on a building and you -- or where -- or how high it was mounted, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So without those -- that data, how can you figure out line of sight to the southern location?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for sure in Vlasenica there is not a single feature that would be higher than the obstacle between the installation and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is the basis of this knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I passed through Vlasenica. I know there are no features that would be higher than 50 metres, which is the difference in altitude on the route towards Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When did you pass through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I passed through before the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I'm looking at the clock. I think it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Gives you a chance to reorganise your thoughts as well. Perhaps you inquire about the 50 metres after the break. Witness, we take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, just to stay briefly, I hope, with this topic of the Vlasenica. Now, do you know Vlasenica well enough to know that there's -- in the vicinity of the town it rises as much as 50 metres from the town -- inside the -- the elevations of the town? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreters didn't hear the answer. So do you know Vlasenica well enough to know that it rises as much as 50 metres from one end of town to the other?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so to get an accurate elevation of the radio relay station, you'd need to know what part of town the radio relay was in, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, the altitude of the station has to be determined with precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And let me read you something that Milenko Jevdjevic said in this courtroom in response to Mr. Ivetic on February 18th, page 31909: "This radio relay route between Veliki Zep and the elevation here, it's called Viselac, above the town of Vlasenica. In Vlasenica that's where the corps command was, in the centre of town, and on the building of the corps command, that is to say, on the roof of that command building, we had an antenna and equipment. Whoever it was that drew this map went here, about a kilometre and a half to the west, and he thought that we had a relay equipment here but we actually had it here in town on the roof-top, on the roof-top of that building." So according to Mr. Jevdjevic, the radio relay station was on the top of the building in the centre of the town of Vlasenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In any event, if the radio relay station was on the top of a building located in the centre of town, you would want to know where in the centre of town so you could determine the ground location, and you would want to know the height of the building in order to know how high up in the air the machines were located. Both those things would be important in figuring out line of sight. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly one does have to know exactly what the altitude is, taking into account -- well, if it's over 20 metres, say, a pole, a building, that has to be taken into account, if it's that tall or taller than that. But below 20 metres, no, when elaborating the profile of the radio relay route.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can go on. Now, let's go to your report again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 1187, page 46. Should be in the English -- excuse me. Page 46 is the Serbian version and English should be 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we'll note in the English, of course, they did not reproduce the map so you just -- you can see the reference under the map, under document number 3, map of disposition of interception stations of the ABiH 2nd Corps. We see the actual map. Now, sir, that's the map that -- isn't that the map that Mr. Ivetic showed you yesterday? He didn't show you a part that was connected to your report. He just showed you the map perhaps for simplicity, but that's the same map that Mr. Ivetic showed you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is what -- partially what some of the things you said about it at page 37804, line 18: "And this is definitely a map that was part of the documents that were received by the commander of the southern facility, and you can see that certain zones were set there, zone number 1, number 2, going from the left to the right, 1, 2, 3, and 4." If you go on the next page, and line 8, you'll say: "So this was -- you could see that it wasn't done very precisely. On the example of the Veliki Zep node, 1 centimetre on the map is actually 1 kilometre actually in the field. So when you look at it here, you could see that the stations are at least 2 kilometres away from each other, but that's not true because all of them were actually clustered at Veliki Zep." The next page, 37806. No, actually, I think that's enough. You agreed with me that yesterday you were critical of this map, of its -- of what it -- of how it was created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, last week. Time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So, sir, we -- let me ask you again. Do you recall - and perhaps you had a chance to think about this because you heard what I said last week - do you recall that this map was actually a map that was part of the -- Rodic's appendix in his report, which is in this record at 65 ter 32891? Do you remember that? That's where you pulled this map from?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I got the map from the law office and not within the analysis of Djuro Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But you'll agree with me that you had a chance to review Rodic's full report and you actually cited the annexes in your report.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, this map coming out of the annex that you cited, if one looks carefully at this map and the other maps in the entire record, it's clear, from the Prosecution's view, that this map was actually created and the handwriting on it is Mr. Rodic's, and that is not a map of the Muslim forces. Now taking into consideration that this was a map created by Mr. Rodic, do you want to change your comments regarding this map?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't change my opinion, sir. I said that this was part of an order to the commander of this southern facility and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, I -- having marked Rodic's reports, Mr. President, we'll decide whether we offer those into evidence on this point. But in any event, I will go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we've already talked briefly about when written documents are sent over the radio relay devices, if they're encoded, as you've said, they could not be intercepted, and if they went out in the free they could be. Let's go to -- I want to now show you some intercepts to get your view on some of these intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 65 ter 32834. And this is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, what this is, as you can see, it's from the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's entitled a report, and it's sending the information which in this case is -- are the two different transmissions. The first one we can see was intercepted on the 14th of March at 2151 hours at a frequency of 785.000, and we note that it appears to be a document to the Drina Corps command, Captain Novakovic. And it about UNHCR convoys, and it's under the name of Mile Maksimovic. And 785.000, that would be a RRU-800 communication; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Or FM-200.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now let's go to another document, 65 ter 32833. I'm told it's not there. If we could get a second, Ms. Stewart might help me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
