utterances.text: When it does come, is it also under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, it should be appearing soon. But you'll see it's a document that we actually picked up from one of the document collections which we have an original of. It's from the Zvornik Brigade. It's practically identical, as you can see, to what was intercepted. And even the time received is 2150, and the intercept noted time of interception 2151. So would you agree with me that the ABiH was able to actually intercept this communication and get the full document or get the document as we see it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know on the basis of this document what radio relay route was used for intercepting this. As you said, however, if it was open, then certainly it can be read this way. Had it been encoded, that would have been impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the intercept of the previous page does not give the relay route but it does give the frequency, 785.000. So is it fair to say if this is an actual intercept by the Muslims, then it would show that they were able to intercept at frequency 785.000?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio relay frequency of 785, that is FM-200 and others, whether it was encoded or not, it doesn't matter. It can certainly be heard. If they know how to decode it, fine; if not, they cannot. But I don't see the frequency here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go back to 32834 which is not -- that one does -- should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So I'm sure you see the same text and you see the actual frequency and time at which it was intercepted. Okay. So just to -- you agree with me it was the frequency 785.000, that was where they were, according to the Muslims, picking this up so ...

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what they claim, then that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, how could they have faked this?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert in that field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to the next page in this document, this report, and the next page, there's a note at the top and it says: "This same telegram intercepted on 10 kilohertz." And then it has another long -- this time a long intercept that says "UNPROFOR" on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And could we go to the next page of this intercept. And the next page. And the next page. Okay. And we see it's under the name of Milovanovic. Now, let's go to -- and I'll offer this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Let's first go to the last page in B/C/S so that the witness has the chance to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and there can you see it's Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I will offer this packet in a group. All right. So now that we've seen that intercept, can we go to 65 ter 24784.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd like in English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently there's some problem in opening. Is that the English version which is not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's try 65 ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, here is another -- this is an original Main Staff -- that we have the original Main Staff document. It's what we call a convoy report that we've got from our collections that, as you can see, it closely resembles the intercept that we just saw, and we note that it -- up in the left-hand corner under Main Staff it says "text in clear." What does that mean, "text in clear?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who processes the document is the one who says whether it's going to be encoded or not. We can see here that the person processing the document asked that it not be encoded, that it be open.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So would that mean if the Muslim intercepters are able to enter the beam of this communication, they could get this document as they did?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so if this intercept is true, the Muslims -- Muslim forces in the intercept that we just looked at, at 32834, said it was captured at frequency 897.000. That would also then be an active frequency used by the VRS for sending this kind of document; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So I would offer 32834, which is the intercept report with both the intercepts, and then the document of the shorter intercept, which is 32833.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page of the B/C/S of this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And lastly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic asked to be able to see the last page of this document in the original. Mr. Ivetic, no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And then finally the document 24874, which is the actual UN convoy document that matches that intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 32834 receives Exhibit Number P7500, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 32833 receives Exhibit Number P7501.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 24784 receives Exhibit Number P7502, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. And that last one should also not be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness raised his hand. He wants to say something. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this document was not sent through radio relay communications of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it has a stamp. And that cannot be sent that way. Only by fax.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. That's a good point.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or it was obtained in some other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me go to 65 ter 32887. And we don't have an English for this, Mr. President, but it is, as you can tell, fundamentally this -- the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Witness, can you now look at this document and let's look at the end of it. This is an actual teletype, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am familiar with the shape of the lettering, this was typewritten on a typewriter, not a teleprinter. At least not a VRS teleprinter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I think we'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I would offer this into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On this one, I think I will object since we haven't had any, I think, substantive linkage of this to the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The witness rightly pointed out that the first document I showed him was a signed and -- a signed document that we received and so this is the same document, as you can tell, and it's the Prosecution's position that this is a teletype. And so it's directly related to responding to the witness's appropriate comment and gives the Trial Chamber the kind of information they need when looking at these intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The last section of this document, at least in my reading of it, is not the same text as was the last section of the document we just looked at, so I would take issue with that. I just glanced at the last paragraph on the last page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last paragraph, paragraph 13, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, on the previous document which has now been admitted as P7502. My quick glance at that does not seem to comport to the text that is contained on this document. Nor does the signature appear to have the same text that was in that document. So for counsel to represent that it's the same document is, I think, a foundational leap that we're not at this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can have them --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Side by side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- in B/C/S side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, we know an original document gets sent to the teletypist and he will type that into -- we've learned this before, type that in the decoding teletype machine, and they may not and they have not always been identical when we have originals versus what gets tapped into the machine. But any careful look at this - and I'm sorry we don't have it in English - will show that this the -- basically the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's a difference --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- convoy document --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's a difference between basically the same, the same, identical, we've gone full circle now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we're not talking finger-prints here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we look at the last page in the B/C/S version which is on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, the one on the right, sorry. And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and now we would like to go back to the original one to the left-hand side we saw first. That's the teletyped version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which is 65 ter 32887.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, and to assist Your Honours, there's the part that starts "napo nema." That I believe is not present in the version that we are now calling up, so in the large capital --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, let's see ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where is "napo nema"? It's just --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's the third line from the end of the text, Your Honours. It's in capital letters and says: "NAPO NEMA," and that text is missing from the copy on the left as is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether it's missing or not, it's not legible --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's not -- it's not legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear -- it's clear that there are a few lines following which have very bad legibility. To say that it's missing is perhaps one step too far because the line before "napo nema" seems to be there. I see a number, 4889, still being there. And you can see that there is some text illegible there. And then as far as the signature is concerned, we see that on the -- what is claimed to be the teletyped version, we see Manojlo Milovanovic, and that's seems to be approximately the same as what we see under the stamp under the signed version.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Not really. On the signed version there is two additional lines of information that are not visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, are not visible, not visible, but what is visible --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- seems to be similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. And for the teletyped version, we're waiting for the translation therefore it will be MFI'd. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 32887 will receive Exhibit Number P7503, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification, pending translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Back to your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: D1187. Should be page 31 in the English, page 45 in the Serbian. Not to be broadcast, I think, just to be on the safe side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have English on the right-hand side of the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, what I wanted to ask you about is this -- the paragraph that starts: "Most of the Drina Corps communications ..." Which I hope is on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll resume at quarter to 2.00. Whether we'll then turn into private session again, yes or no, is still uncertain at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you know how you're going proceed or not? Or did you discuss the matter with Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We did, and I think we have a general idea aside from chaos which we know is always lurking behind us. But the -- regarding the disclosure, any disclosure issue, the original info report was this phone conversation where we -- Mr. Blaszczyk interviewed the person over the -- Kostic over the phone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I was mainly interested in how you would proceed in court and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, the idea was that there's a couple of points which I don't think are really very contested by the Defence that this person tells us in both the info report and the statement that have to do with the authenticity of the intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, and I'm not going to offer the documents into evidence, just the -- but some of the key information in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what we discussed and I can clarify that there were several information reports and the reference to the statement only came in the last one which is dated 11 August 2015.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that substantially different from what is in the information report?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The statement, there are some differences, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But that's the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was not whether there are some differences but whether it's substantially different. But you say on details or.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On details. I have not gone through it line by line, Your Honours. We were trying to figure out how to get this going, but I think we can proceed in the manner that Mr. McCloskey has indicated. That's what I think is the main thrust for us at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, so if we could have this statement on the board, 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're in open session. I don't think if that makes any difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't -- perhaps since we started in private we should just continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll again move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'm addressing the Defence in this item. The Chamber also invites the Prosecution by the same date to give a provisional indication of whether, what kind, and how much rebuttal evidence it intends to present.
